faqs.q: What should I include on a tile job estimate?
faqs.a: At minimum: your business name and license number, the client and job-site address, a dated line-item list (installation per sq ft, labor, grouting, demo, waterproofing, materials), a validity date, deposit terms, and exclusions. Note that the estimate is not a final invoice — final charges may vary with substrate condition and layout complexity.

faqs.q: How do I estimate a tile job?
faqs.a: Measure the square footage of each surface to be tiled (length × height for walls, length × width for floors). Multiply by your per-sq-ft installation rate, then add labor hours, grouting, demo, waterproofing, and materials. Add 10–15% waste allowance for cuts and breakage. Put each on its own line so the customer can see the breakdown.

faqs.q: Is this template free to use?
faqs.a: Yes. All three formats (PDF, Word, Excel) are free to download with no email required.

faqs.q: Does the Excel version calculate the deposit automatically?
faqs.a: Yes. Enter your quantities and rates, and the subtotal, 25% deposit and balance due update automatically.

faqs.q: Is this legal or tax advice?
faqs.a: No. Templates are for informational purposes only. Requirements vary by state — verify with your contractor board and a CPA or attorney before use.
